# Rear swing arm hinge replacement and bushing service

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Replace rear swing arm hinge bushings by separating components, pressing in new parts, and polishing for snug fit. [t199]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the rear bumper or swing arm assembly from the vehicle.
2. Separate the swing arm from the mounting bracket by cutting off nuts and bolts if seized.
3. Use a 20-ton press to separate the bushing/bolt assembly from the swing arm.

_Procedure reported by [t199]._

## Tools

- 20-ton hydraulic press [t199]
- [Partial] 1-inch socket or wrench [t199]
- [Partial] Breaker bar (optional) [t199]

## Parts

- Bushing with grease fitting [t199]
- Swing arm hinge kit [t199]
- Washer and 1" bolt with locknut [t199]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Drill a hole in the swing arm to accept a zerk (grease fitting) for future lubrication. [t199]
- Polish the inside of the pressed-in bushing so it accepts the bolt snugly, as pressing tightens the ID. [t199]

## Common mistakes

- Using an oversized socket that breaks under leverage and flattening the top of the bolt instead of turning it. [t199]
- [Partial] Forgetting to separate the nut from the bottom before trying to remove a seized upper bolt. [t199]
